title: Read a log in chunks

blocks.md:
## Chunks, not one giant string in your head

`fs.createReadStream` fires `data` as pieces arrive. You collect those pieces, then join them when `end` fires. You do not assume the first chunk is the whole file.

This fixture is small. You still practice the API: collect, join, take the last non-empty line (`east`). The hidden test also checks that your source mentions `createReadStream`.

The night log drips in. The first line is `north`. The fox’s last heading is `east` — print that, not the first drip.

blocks.promptMd: You know the file is finished when…
The first `data` event means the whole file is already in memory.
blocks.explainMd: data can fire more than once. end is the signal that no more chunks are coming.

blocks.promptMd: > Stream `chunk-log.txt`, print the last trimmed line (`east`).

hintLadder.md: Open a read stream on `chunk-log.txt`. Collect text as `data` fires.
On `end`, split into lines and take the last non-empty one.
Listen for data and end. Hidden wants createReadStream in the source.
